monthly.summary: Kaguguta Agrifarm recorded 40.8mm of rain in August 2026, roughly 0.9 times the long-term August average of around 48mm and in line with what is typical for the month. Rain fell on 12 days, of which 6 exceeded 1mm, and the final dekad accounted for 28.3mm of the monthly total across 7 rainy days. Rainfall was concentrated at the end of the month, with 19.0mm falling between 29 and 31 August, including the month's heaviest day on 30 August at 15.4mm; heavy rainfall also fell on 22 August (8.1mm) and 5 August (5.0mm). Kenya Meteorological Department forecasts had called for near-average to below-average August rainfall over Kilifi and the rest of the coast, and the WMO and ICPAC reported a strengthening El Niño with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole likely, with ICPAC forecasting wetter-than-normal conditions for October to December.

Kaguguta Agrifarm recorded 122.8mm of rain in September 2026, roughly 3.5 times the long-term September average of around 35mm and well above normal for the month. Rain fell on 23 days, with 11 days above 1mm and 5 days above 10mm, and the wettest spell ran from 17 to 21 September, when 58.7mm fell in five days, including 42.3mm between 18 and 20 September. The three heaviest days were 11 September at 27.7mm, 18 September at 24.1mm and 27 September at 20.2mm, and the middle ten days of the month accounted for 74.5mm of the total. The Kenya Meteorological Department had forecast near-average September rainfall for Kilifi and the rest of the southern Coast, so the station total ran well above that outlook. Kenya Met reported the Indian Ocean Dipole at around +0.7°C in late September, with a peak near +1.0°C expected in October, and the WMO and ICPAC expect a positive IOD and strengthening El Niño to bring a wetter-than-normal October to December season to the region.

daily_narrative: KILIFI, Kenya, Oct 7 - Kaguguta Agrifarm weather station recorded 5.04 mm of rainfall on Oct 6, following 0.56 mm on Oct 5 and three dry days from Oct 2 to Oct 4. The station has logged 6.7 mm so far in the first dekad of October, which is also the month's total to date. The ECMWF ensemble forecast points to a mean of 2.9 mm for Oct 7, with a 75th percentile of 3.4 mm. Rainfall is expected to increase on Oct 8, with a forecast mean of 20.8 mm and a 75th percentile of 27.6 mm.
dekadal_narrative: Rainfall for the dekad totalled 37.7 mm over 8 rainy days, which was more than Sep-D1 at 10.6 mm but less than Sep-D2 at 74.5 mm. Two days accounted for most of the total: 20.2 mm fell on 27 September, with an instantaneous peak rate of 53 mm/h at 08:42 and a maximum 1-hour accumulation of 5.0 mm, and 15.0 mm fell on 21 September, together making up about 93% of the dekad. The remaining days each recorded 1.1 mm or less, and 25 and 26 September were dry. The forecast for the next dekad points to a wetter period, with a total of 165.1 mm and the heaviest falls expected from 12 to 14 October, peaking at 38.6 mm on 13 October. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is developing, with the Bureau of Meteorology's weekly index at +0.76°C for the week ending 27 September, above the +0.4°C threshold for a third consecutive week, and this phase tends to enhance short-rains rainfall over East Africa; KMSA's October-December outlook accordingly favours above-average rainfall for Kilifi.
